uses.reason: the operand matcher's own rule (`extra.knownOnly`: only a word of known text is an extra operand of find's late path), which places the roles `refusalOf` reads
another field of the same name: the query functions bazel refuses in a command (`refuses` of its own table), not a spec's
the runner gives up on an extra operand: no example runs a refused line (`refusedIn`), so it is reached where no refusal is said (words not all known, `basename a b "$x"`)
the same for date (`date +%F "$x"`): no example where a word may be an extra operand date refuses
